Limits: Registered guest already-connected remote PID sends use owned ordered publication, producer cancellation and generation isolation. Full option validation precedes state checks; connected noconnect may send. Immediate nosuspend conservatively returns WouldSuspend when capacity or captured sequential-trace state prevents admission, without advancing the token. Negotiated sender, trace and priority controls are bounded SDK adaptations; native scheduler phase parity is not claimed. Disconnected/pending autoconnect, remote named destinations/aliases and synchronous embedding helpers remain incomplete. SDK HOST/controller and original-only observations are separate; no live SDK-peer or native wire equality is claimed. With process_flag(async_dist,true), already-connected PID sends use bounded entry-owned accepted packet staging: accepted output survives sender death, retains original order and contributes staged plus transport AccountedBytes to dist_get_stat SendPend. False retains producer-owned319 behavior. A full independent staging budget raises system_limit before acceptance, including send_nosuspend; it is an SDK cap, not a native busy threshold or physical-memory measurement. Original new flag cases and live SDK-peer comparison remain separate gates. Caller-owned already-connected output waits now serially admit existing owner control signals and system queries while waiting for ticket turn or transport capacity, preserving ordinary message receive order and existing nested-wait guards. Cancellation or inbound kill settles producer reservations before completion. Accepted UNLINK workers remain connection-owned; only the guest wait admits its caller signals, without canceling retained output. Immediate nosuspend and accepted async staging do not gain capacity waits. Pending/autoconnect, synchronous embedding setters, complete inbound priority, live SDK peers and native scheduler/wire equality remain incomplete.

Limits: Single direct contract case plus feature regressions; complete error/options and OTP differential verification pending Already-connected guest remote PID unlink suppresses the local relation before a captured-generation UNLINK_ID is accepted by the connection-owned worker. Accepted unlink output survives producer death and joins global output drain; ACK and stale EXIT identities preserve relink state. Duplicate unlink is idempotent; pending/autoconnect, a live SDK network peer and native wire equality remain incomplete. Caller-owned already-connected output waits now serially admit existing owner control signals and system queries while waiting for ticket turn or transport capacity, preserving ordinary message receive order and existing nested-wait guards. Cancellation or inbound kill settles producer reservations before completion. Accepted UNLINK workers remain connection-owned; only the guest wait admits its caller signals, without canceling retained output. Immediate nosuspend and accepted async staging do not gain capacity waits. Pending/autoconnect, synchronous embedding setters, complete inbound priority, live SDK peers and native scheduler/wire equality remain incomplete.
